info.bio:
LCD Soundsystem es un grupo de Dance-Punk y Alternative Dance neoyorquino formado por James Murphy y Tim Goldsworthy. En las actuaciones en vivo, se les une Nancy Whang al teclado y a los coros, Pat Mahoney a la batería, Tyler Pope al bajo y Phil Mossman a la guitarra, a la percusión y al bajo. Murphy y Goldsworthy son también conocidos como el equipo de productores The DFA, y propietarios del sello del mismo nombre.

Es impresionante como cada legado es vuelto a retomar y como en esencia es identificable.

scenes.name: Renacimiento neopostpunk
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Con el nuevo milenio, hipsters hastiados de las discotecas buscan tensión en lugar de catarsis: reediciones de Cabaret Voltaire, Throbbing Gristle, 23 Skidoo, ESG, DNA y Scritti Politti, clubes de punk funk y electropop, reuniones de Gang of Four y Mission of Burma, las películas 24 Hour Party People y Control, y bandas como The Rapture, LCD Soundsystem, Franz Ferdinand, Interpol, Liars, !!!, Wolf Eyes y Bloc Party. Dominan las inflexiones de la militancia postpunk, pero no su compromiso: lo más valioso de aquella época era su fe en el cambio, «que la música podía importar tanto».

podcast.title: Local Hit (2001-2005)
podcast.body: After forming in 2001, LCD Sound System became a local hit in New York, though broader recognition didn't come until their 2005 debut album. "In 2001, he started up his own band, LCD Sound System. They were something of a local hit..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Alt Rock Success in the 2000s
podcast.body: LCD Soundsystem was one of several acts that blended alt rock sensibilities with various dance influences, achieving alt rock hits during the 2000s. This represented a revival of the dance-oriented alternative attitude seen in the 1980s. "But now we also had LCD sound system...They all had alt rock hits in the odds."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: David Bowie's Admiration
podcast.body: David Bowie was deeply impressed by LSD SoundSystem from the release of their first album, considering them a major reference in modern music. This admiration led him to invite the band's leader, James Murphy, to co-produce his final album, Black Star. "David Bowie está maravillado desde que sale el primer disco del LSD SoundSystem y lo tiene como una de las grandes referencias en la música moderna."

podcast.title: Hipster Music Association
podcast.body: This band was popular among those identifying with hipster culture in the 2010s, aligning with tastes for older or retro sounds. "If that was your scene, I'm going to bet that you and your like-minded friends could also agree on indie era radiohead, LCD sound system, bright eyes, arcade fire, willko, tame and pala, body bear, fleet foxes, and these guys, who were so intertwined with hipster culture, that they actually became a meme."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Influence from The Strokes
podcast.body: LCD Sound System was explicitly named as one of the bands that credit The Strokes as a significant influence on their musical style. "Other bands crediting the strokes as an influence include Arctic Monkeys, Franz Ferdinand, and LCD Sound System."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Key Figure in New York Indie Rock Revival
podcast.body: LCD Sound System became a prominent band in the New York indie rock revival, a scene that also featured groups such as The Strokes, Yeah Yeah Yeahs, and Interpol. "LCD Sound System was one of the leading lights of the New York indie rock revival that also included bands like The Strokes and The Ye-Ye-As and Interpol."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Professed Krautrock Fans
podcast.body: The members of LCD Sound System are cited as professing their admiration for Krautrock, demonstrating the genre's influence extending into modern electronic and dance-rock. "Other profess fans of crop rock include the members of Radiohead, Sonic Youth and LCD Sound System."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Declined Seinfeld Scriptwriting Job
xref.body: James Murphy was once offered a job as a scriptwriter for the popular TV show *Seinfeld*. He turned down this opportunity to instead continue pursuing his music career, which ultimately led to the formation of LCD Soundsystem. "James Murphy was once offered a job as a script writer for Seinfeld, but he turned that down in favor of sticking with music, which resulted in LCD sound system."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind-Blowing Facts About Music in 60 Minutes: 2017 Edition

xref.title: NYC Indie Scene Prominence
xref.body: TV on the Radio was a significant part of the New York City indie music scene in the early 2000s, a period that also saw the rise of bands like the Yeah Yeah Yeahs, The Strokes, The Rapture, and LCD Soundsystem. "TV on the radio was a major part of the New York City indie scene in the early 2000s. This was the same scene that gave us the yay-yayah as the strokes, the rapture and LCD sound system."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
